title: Whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever, however

seo.title: Whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever, however - Test-English
seo.description: Learn how to use whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever and however in this B1+ grammar lesson with rules, charts and exercises. Practise now!

Exercise 3

Complete the sentences with whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever, however or whichever.
explanation:
It doesn’t matter what, when, where, etc.

When we add -ever after what, which, when, where, who or how, we create a new word that means that any choice is possible. For example, if we say, ‘You can sit wherever you want,’ we mean that you can sit in any place available, and it doesn’t matter which place you choose.

In the grammar chart below, you can see the meanings of these words and example sentences.

Whatever

It means ‘anything’ or ‘everything’, ‘it doesn’t matter what’. For example, if we say, ‘Do whatever you like,’ we mean that you can do anything from all the possible things, it doesn’t matter which.

  • You can be whatever you want to be; the only thing you need is hard work.
  • I am very proud of all of you, whatever happens in the game tomorrow.

Whichever

Whichever is similar to whatever, but we use it when we have a limited number of options. It means ‘anyone (of a number of options)’, ‘it doesn’t matter which’.

  • You can retire at 65 or after 40 years of employment, whichever arrives first.
  • The prize is a trip to one of our five available destinations. Choose whichever you prefer. 

Whenever

It means ‘at any time’ or ‘at every time’, ‘it doesn’t matter when’. If we say, ‘You can come whenever you want,’ we mean that you can come at any time you want from all the possible times; it doesn’t matter when.

  • I just go there whenever they tell me. 
  • I can meet you tomorrow or whenever is more convenient for you.

Wherever

It means ‘at any place’ or ‘at every place’, ‘it doesn’t matter where’.

  • Be friendly, and you will find new friends wherever you go. 
  • Technology allows many people to work from wherever they want.

Whoever

It means ‘any person who’, ‘it doesn’t matter who’. If we say, ‘Whoever finishes first is going to win a prize,’ we mean that from all the people, any person who finishes first, it doesn’t matter who, is going to win a prize.

  • Police are looking for whoever was responsible for this heinous crime. 
  • Whoever did this is going to pay for it. 

However

It means ‘in any way’, ‘it doesn’t matter how’. It can be used in some different contexts, in which we could also find the word how without ever.

  • When you buy your own house, you can customise it however you want. (=You can customise it in any way you want; it doesn’t matter how.)
  • However much you think it costs, triple that amount. (=It doesn’t matter how much you think it costs.)
